texts: mixed: the full-moon state is reified and also kept in plain form, and Year 1 lands, but 'day 68 of Year 1' is recorded as a day-of-month numbered 68 — the only day term we have is the day inside a month — so the day-of-year reading is lost and this date will not order against other dates in the same year. If your calendar has month names, date it with a month plus a day inside that month: 'On the <n>th of <month-name>, Year 1, the moon was full.'
good. the Council and the Watch are both treated as definite common-noun referents, and the convening carries its agent, its location and past tense.
good. 'sky-cat drought' is kept as one kind and unpacked to its genus 'drought', the Council reuses the symbol introduced in the previous sentence, and the drought sits in the right object role.

good. the report gets Tessa as its holder and the Council as its recipient, and the claim about the store is sealed — recorded as something reported, not asserted as fact — with 'would be' kept as future relative to the reporting.

mixed: the discussion, the Council, the ration and 'for the winter' all land, but 'stricter' is dropped outright: a comparative with no stated standard has no licensed form, so the record says only that a plain feather ration was discussed and the whole point of the sentence is gone. Name what it is stricter than: 'The Council discussed a feather ration for the winter that was stricter than the current ration.'

good. the whole report is sealed as reported rather than asserted, 'also' is kept as an additive marker on the coming, and both the ordering of the thin autumn before the bad winter and the twenty-six-year distance are carried.

mixed: the recording, the Council and the ledger are all fine, but 'the observation' has no antecedent to attach to, so it mints a brand-new, unconnected entity and what was actually written down is lost. Name the report or finding it refers to, so it links back to the earlier sentence: 'The Council recorded Old Vesh's report in the ledger.'
